summary: A neighbourhood Diwali evening for about 300 residents in Pune on a ₹50,000 budget (roughly ₹167 a head), centred on a lane-by-lane rangoli contest, a community faral potluck and a short cultural programme on a small stage. Because the budget is tight we assumed a society courtyard or open ground with no venue fee, a resident-run potluck covering most of the food, and eco-friendly fireworks only if the society and local police allow it. With about six weeks to go, permissions and sponsorship should start immediately.

budget.tips: Use string lights in warm white, marigold toran and hand-made diyas from a local potter. Ask residents to lend lanterns and large rangoli stencils.
Run a faral potluck where each household brings one traditional item such as chakli, karanji or ladoo. Pay only for chai, water and a large pot of khichdi or misal for volunteers.
Rent a basic PA system for four hours instead of a full stage setup, and invite resident children and local bhajan or dhol groups to perform for a small honorarium.
Choose a short, licensed green-cracker display or a lantern release, and keep a fire extinguisher and sand buckets ready beside it.
Get the society NOC and the loudspeaker permission from the local police station early, and borrow a first aid kit from the nearest clinic.
Promote through the society WhatsApp groups and a few printed A3 posters at the gates and lifts rather than flex banners.
Run diya-painting and rangoli contests with prizes sponsored by local shops, and use recycled material for craft stations.
Give volunteers simple coloured armbands or sashes instead of t-shirts and cover their refreshments from the potluck leftovers.
Place segregated wet, dry and compost bins at every food stall and tie in with the society housekeeping staff for a quick post-event clean-up.
Hold this back for rain cover, an extra generator hour or a last-minute sound fix.

timeline.task: Form a small organising committee and assign leads for food, decor, programme, safety and publicity
Apply for the society NOC and the local police loudspeaker and fireworks permissions
Approach local shops and businesses for sponsorship and in-kind prizes
Collect voluntary household contributions and open a simple shared expense sheet
Book the sound system, string lights and the stage platform with the rental vendor
Launch publicity: WhatsApp invites, A3 posters and a volunteer sign-up form
Finalise the programme: kids' dance, bhajan set, rangoli contest and diya-painting
Share the faral potluck sign-up sheet and confirm tea and snack vendors
Buy diyas, torans, rangoli colours and prizes
Create the volunteer roster and hold a safety briefing on crowd flow and emergency contacts
Arrange first aid, fire extinguishers, ramps and seating for senior citizens
Do a site walkthrough and a full sound and lighting check with the vendor
Put up the string lights, torans and signage around the courtyard
Mark the rangoli areas, set up the stage and confirm every volunteer's slot
Run the Diwali evening: Lakshmi Pujan, rangoli judging, performances, faral sharing and the fireworks finale
Clean up, return rentals, share the final expense sheet and thank sponsors and volunteers

checklist: Compare rental rates for string lights and confirm the number of metres needed
Order marigold toran and diyas from a local supplier
Confirm electrical points, extension cables and a safe load
Plan the set-up and take-down timings with volunteers
Share the faral potluck sheet and assign items to avoid duplicates
Book chai and water for volunteers and senior guests
Arrange serving tables, hand-wash points and disposable or steel plates
Plan separate bins for wet and dry waste
Rent a PA system with two microphones for four hours
Confirm the stage size and the performance running order
Check permitted sound hours and keep the volume within limits
Arrange a backup extension and spare batteries
Confirm that green crackers or a lantern release are allowed by the society and police
Mark a safe distance zone and keep children behind a barrier
Keep a fire extinguisher, sand and water buckets in place
Assign two trained volunteers to the display
Get the society NOC in writing
Submit the loudspeaker application to the local police station
Prepare a basic first aid kit and the numbers for the nearest clinic
Share an emergency contact sheet with all volunteers

ideas.title: Lane-by-lane rangoli contest
ideas.description: Give each building or lane a rangoli patch and a theme such as 'Light and Unity'. Residents judge each other's work and the winning lane gets a trophy diya.

ideas.title: Faral potluck table
ideas.description: Every household brings a homemade Diwali item such as chakli, karanji or ladoo. Label them and serve them together so the whole neighbourhood tastes everyone's recipe.

ideas.title: Diya-painting for kids
ideas.description: Set up a table with plain clay diyas, acrylic paints and glitter so children can paint one to keep and one to place on the entrance decoration.

ideas.title: Lantern walk
ideas.description: Let residents make akash kandils in a pre-event workshop and walk through the lanes at dusk, ending with a short Lakshmi Pujan at the courtyard.

ideas.title: Green Diwali pledge wall
ideas.description: Put up a large chart where families sign a pledge to use fewer crackers, reduce noise and segregate waste, with a small token of appreciation for every signature.
